canonical_name: Ford-Fulkerson minimal-cut theorem for finite undirected networks
canonical_statement: For every finite undirected graph with distinct source and sink vertices and a strictly positive real capacity on each graph arc, there are a maximal feasible finite nonnegative weighted collection of non-self-intersecting source-to-sink chains and a minimum disconnecting arc set whose values are equal.

source_selection.citation: L. R. Ford, Jr. and D. R. Fulkerson, Maximal Flow Through a Network, Canadian Journal of Mathematics 8 (1956), 399-404, DOI 10.4153/CJM-1956-045-5
source_selection.relationship_to_catalog: The source theorem is a direct theorem-family match for the catalog equality gloss. This phase selects the source's finite undirected, nonnegative weighted chain-flow and disconnecting-set formulation rather than silently replacing it with directed edge flows and conservation.
source_selection.review_boundary: The exact source-shaped formal proposition is frozen, but repository source identity, the historical word 'number' to NNReal representation, complete correction and errata review, proof-node mapping, and independent H0 approval remain open.

domain_and_universes: At arbitrary universes uV and uE: finite ambient vertex and arc types V and E; G : Graph V E; source sink : V; capacity : E -> NNReal; Chain G source sink; finitely supported nonnegative chain weights; Finset E disconnecting sets.
hypotheses: source and sink belong to G.vertexSet
0 < capacity arc for every arc in G.edgeSet
conclusion: There are a feasible flow and disconnecting arc set such that the flow dominates every feasible flow by value, the disconnecting set has value no greater than every disconnecting set, and the two selected values are equal.

encoding_decisions.graph: Mathlib Graph V E, an undirected multigraph substrate with finite ambient vertex and edge types; graph vertices and arcs remain explicit subsets of those finite types
encoding_decisions.terminals: Both terminals lie in G.vertexSet and are distinct
encoding_decisions.chain: A positive length, injective ordered vertex array and injective ordered arc array with consecutive Graph.IsLink witnesses and fixed source/sink endpoints
encoding_decisions.capacity_and_weight_domain: NNReal, the subtype of nonnegative real numbers; graph-arc capacities are strictly positive, while chain-flow weights may be zero
encoding_decisions.flow: Finsupp from source-to-sink chains to NNReal, exactly matching the paper's finite coordinate collection after repeated equal chains are combined
encoding_decisions.feasibility: For each graph arc, the sum of every component value whose chain uses that arc is at most its capacity
encoding_decisions.disconnecting_set: A finite set containing only graph arcs and meeting every source-to-sink chain, not merely every chain in the selected flow support
encoding_decisions.extrema: The conclusion supplies witnesses and universally compares them with every feasible flow and every disconnecting set; it does not assume optimization data
encoding_decisions.boundary: Networks with no source-to-sink chain are included; the definitions make zero flow and the empty disconnecting set the intended witnesses, but this statement phase adds no boundary proof. Parallel arcs, isolated vertices, and ambient nonvertices/nonedges are allowed. Graph loops are inert because injective-vertex chains cannot use them; whether the historical graph convention excluded them remains an H1 transport question.

minimal_import_result: Deleting any one of the three direct imports makes the exact module fail. They respectively supply finitely supported finite sums, undirected multigraph incidence, and the nonnegative-real coefficient domain. No max-flow theorem or proof-bearing network-flow module is imported.

checked_alternate_encodings.boundary: This is a direct source-shaped respelling with the same helper definitions and sequenced hypotheses. No transport to directed edge-flow/conservation, Real-valued predicates, vertex-partition cuts, or supremum/infimum encodings is credited.

equality of supremum and infimum without attained witnesses
inclusion-minimal cuts rather than all disconnecting sets
